originality.rationale: Best-knowledge claim is the exact zero-inflated geometric edge triangular-face incidence law for pooled uniform vertex-or-edge RRSC(2), not the general exponential face-degree phenomenon. The motivating accessible paper descriptions cover vertex degrees and simplex counts; an earlier distinct pure-edge triangle-growth paper derives exponential incidence but has no zero-incidence edge stratum. Earlier face-dimension selection/preferential models have different rules and power-law generalised degrees. The motivating full primary text remains unavailable and creates priority risk.
residual_risks: The motivating exact-model original arXiv full text could not be accessed; a nonindexed edge-incidence theorem may appear there.
Earlier fixed-dimension exponential edge-degree theory could be adaptable by a more general unlocated theorem.
Two related face-dimension growth papers had only abstracts/excerpts accessible, so precise coverage of special nonpreferential cases is unresolved.
No independent literature-priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: The complete empirical triangle-incidence law of an edge is a natural local invariant for a random simplicial complex whose vertex degrees are known to have a power-law tail. The exact positive zero-incidence mass, q1=3/5 single-incidence fraction and geometric positive tail describe a structural contrast directly relevant to higher-order attachment and not implied by global face counts or vertex-degree frequencies. It is a natural complete classification for this observable, not an arbitrary low-dimensional numerical slice.
